0:0.en: My name is Kasia and I live in Krakow.

0:1.en: I get up at seven every day.

0:2.en: First I take a shower, and then I eat breakfast.

0:3.en: I usually eat bread with cheese and drink tea with lemon.

1:0.en: I leave home at eight o'clock.

1:1.en: I'm going to work by tram because I don't have a car.

1:2.en: I work in a small bookstore near the Market Square.

2:0.en: I like my job because I love books.

2:2.en: My dog's name is Pączek and he is very happy.

2:1.en: After work I go for a walk with the dog.

2:3.en: In the evening I read or watch a movie.

0:2.en: I am now in Gdańsk at my grandma's.

0:3.en: Her apartment is small, but very pretty.

1:1.en: In the morning the sun shines, and in the afternoon it rains a little.

1:2.en: We go to the seaside every day.

1:3.en: The water is cold, but the beach is beautiful.

2:1.en: Today for lunch there are pierogi with cheese, and for dessert there is apple pie.

2:2.en: Tomorrow we are going to the Old Town and to the museum.

0:0.en: Last Saturday I went to the market with my mom.

0:1.en: We got up early because the best vegetables disappear quickly.

0:3.en: At the market there were already many people and everywhere smelled of fresh bread.

1:0.en: First we bought tomatoes, cucumbers, and a kilogram of strawberries.

1:1.en: The salesperson was very kind and gave me one strawberry to try.

1:3.en: Then mom bought eggs, honey, and white cheese from a village lady.

2:0.en: At the end I saw a flower stall.

0:2.en: The weather was beautiful and the sun was shining.

2:1.en: I wanted to buy peonies, but I no longer had any money.

2:3.en: Mom smiled and paid for a small bouquet.

3:0.en: We walked home with heavy bags.

3:1.en: In the afternoon we made strawberry pierogi together.

3:2.en: It was a very successful Saturday.

0:0.en: Yesterday evening I heard a strange noise behind the wall.

0:1.en: Someone was walking around in the apartment next door, even though no one had lived there for a year.

0:2.en: I was a bit scared, but I was also curious.

1:0.en: I went out into the hallway and knocked on the door.

1:2.en: I knocked again and then I heard a quiet voice: “Come in!”

1:3.en: The door was open, so I went inside.

2:0.en: There was no furniture or people in the room.

2:1.en: Only a large green parrot was sitting on the windowsill.

2:2.en: She looked at me and said: "Good morning!"

3:0.en: I met a new female neighbor on the stairs this morning.

3:1.en: She moved in on Friday, but the furniture will only arrive in a week.

3:2.en: For now, only her parrot lives there.

3:3.en: The female neighbor invited me for coffee.

3:4.en: The parrot obviously asked whether I prefer tea.

1:0.en: I am writing regarding order number 4521, which I placed in your online store on October 2nd.

1:1.en: I ordered winter boots in size 38.

1:2.en: I wanted to have them before my trip to the mountains, which I planned for mid-month.

1:3.en: According to the information on the website, the package was supposed to arrive within three business days.

2:0.en: Unfortunately, the shipment arrived only after two weeks.

2:1.en: Worse still, I found shoes in size 41 in the box, and to make matters worse, in a different color.

2:2.en: I called the hotline twice, but every time I heard that I had to wait for a message.

2:3.en: No one has contacted me until today.

3:0.en: Therefore, I request an exchange of the item for the correct one or a refund.

3:1.en: I can return the wrong shoes at your expense.

3:2.en: If I do not receive a response within seven days, I will report the matter to the consumer ombudsman.

3:3.en: I would be sorry, because I have been buying from you for years and until now I have been satisfied.

4:0.en: I would be grateful for a quick reply.

0:0.en: More and more Poles commute to work by bicycle.

0:1.en: In my city, in Wrocław, new bike paths are built every year, and in the mornings at intersections more cyclists are seen than before.

0:2.en: I think that this is a very good change.

1:0.en: First of all, a bicycle is healthy and cheap.

1:1.en: You don't have to pay for gas or look for a parking spot.

1:2.en: Secondly, during rush hour you often get there faster by it than by car.

1:3.en: If more people left their cars in the garage, traffic jams would be smaller, and the air cleaner.

2:0.en: Of course I understand that not everyone can commute like that.

2:1.en: Someone who lives thirty kilometers from the office or drives children to kindergarten needs a car.

2:2.en: Besides, Polish winter doesn't encourage riding on two wheels.

2:3.en: When it snows with rain, even I take the tram.

3:0.en: Despite that, I think it's worth trying, even in spring and summer.

3:1.en: I started two years ago and I don't regret it.

3:2.en: Next year I will buy myself a better bike, and maybe I will even convince my boss to do the same.

0:0.en: The residents of the small village of Lipowo in Podlasie have been living the fate of a stork for several weeks, which did not fly to Africa for the winter.

0:1.en: Storks usually leave Poland at the end of August and return only in March.

0:2.en: The bird, named Wojtek by the children, injured its wing in summer and did not recover before its flock's departure.

1:0.en: At first, nobody believed that the stork would survive the first frosts.

1:1.en: The village headman, Mr. Henryk Zalewski, decided however to take matters into his own hands.

1:2.en: He rebuilt an old shed, lined it with straw, and installed a heat lamp in it.

1:3.en: We couldn't leave him to fate.

1:4.en: "A stork is almost a family member to us," said our reporter.

2:0.en: The whole village joined the action.

2:1.en: Students from the local school are collecting money for fish, and a retired veterinarian examines an injured wing twice a week.

2:2.en: It also became loud about Wojtek on the internet, where more than one hundred thousand people have already seen his photos.

3:0.en: Ornithologists remind that wild birds should not be fed unnecessarily, but in this case help was necessary.

3:1.en: For now the bird feels well and, as the neighbors joke, eats for two.

3:2.en: If the treatment goes according to plan, Wojtek will return to his nest on the pole by the fire station in the spring.

3:3.en: The residents are rooting for him and already announcing that they will welcome the remaining storks exceptionally ceremoniously.

0:0.en: November does not have a good reputation in Poland.

0:1.en: It is considered a month of grayness, bare branches, and premature twilight that falls before we manage to leave work.

0:2.en: Even its name, which comes from falling leaves, sounds like an announcement of loss.

0:3.en: It's no wonder that most of us would most prefer to sleep through it entirely.

1:0.en: But over the years I am becoming convinced that we are wronging him.

1:1.en: November, stripped of both summer splendor and December glitter, pretends to be nothing.

1:2.en: It does not tempt with promises and does not demand admiration.

1:3.en: It allows, on the other hand, for something that is becoming increasingly difficult at other times of the year, namely, to slow down without consequences.

2:0.en: After all, it begins on the day when we visit the graves of our loved ones in large numbers.

2:1.en: Cemeteries illuminated by thousands of candles inspire reflection even in those who usually avoid lofty contemplations.

2:2.en: There is something deeply soothing in this custom: the awareness that memory is often more lasting than haste, and the absent still belong to our community.

3:0.en: Later weeks favor activities for which we don't want to waste time in the summer.

3:2.en: No one reminds us then that we are wasting beautiful weather.

3:1.en: We return to postponed readings, brew tea with raspberry juice, and lead conversations at the kitchen table that have no practical purpose.

3:3.en: Grandma used to say that in November a person should, following the example of the earth, rest before the next sowing.

4:0.en: I am certainly not claiming that one should pretend to be enthusiastic about rain and mud.

4:1.en: Lack of light can really get even the biggest optimists down.

4:2.en: I merely think that it's worth stopping treating this month like a burdensome waiting room before the holidays.

4:3.en: Perhaps it is precisely in his silence, undisturbed by noise, that it is easiest to hear one's own thoughts.
